item.title: Oil Price Today (November 26): Brent crude rises to $95 as fresh attacks renew supply fears. What are experts saying?
item.description: Crude oil price : Oil prices surged amid rising tensions in West Asia, particularly following the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil export hub. Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy raised alarms about naval mines endangering tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Financial giants Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan urged caution, noting that ongoing geopolitical strife could dramatically affect oil supply and lead to price volatility in global markets.
item.dc:creator: Veer Sharma
item.content:encoded: Oil prices extended their gains for a second consecutive session on Thursday as intensifying hostilities in West Asia renewed concerns over the recovery of crude exports from the region.The rebound was driven by several developments, including attacks on Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi militants. Ras Tanura, the country's main oil export hub, has been among the key targets. Iran has also claimed that several vessels attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz have struck mines.ALSO READ: D-Street poised for a positive start as GIFT Nifty trades firmly higherCrude oil price on November 26Brent crude traded at $94.66 at about 7:30 am. The benchmark had briefly fallen below $90 earlier this week before rebounding. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) was hovering near $84 a barrel after advancing more than 4% over the previous two sessions. Brent ended below the $95 mark on Wednesday.According to a Reuters report, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said on Wednesday that two tankers had hit naval mines, exploded and caught fire after attempting to navigate an unauthorised route.Diplomatic efforts have so far failed to ease tensions. Tehran has informed Washington that normal shipping through the Strait of Hormuz will not resume until its demands are met. These include an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports and a halt to the war on all fronts. Through Qatari mediators, Iran has offered to reopen the waterway within 48 hours if Washington agrees to these conditions. The US, meanwhile, is seeking concessions on Iran's nuclear programme, while Tehran is also demanding sanctions relief and the release of frozen assets.ALSO READ: Stocks in news: LG Electronics, HDFC Bank, Siemens Energy, Lupin and Schaeffler IndiaThe latest recovery in prices comes after a sharp decline earlier this month. Brent had fallen as crude shipments from the Gulf region picked up, while the International Energy Agency (IEA) projected a surplus in the oil market for the current quarter.What are analysts saying?Despite the recent weakness, Goldman Sachs has flagged longer-term risks to global oil supplies. Earlier this month, the bank raised its price forecasts, warning that Brent crude could climb to $140 a barrel in 2027 if Gulf oil production remains significantly below its 2025 average.Goldman Sachs increased its December Brent forecast to $105 a barrel from $90 previously. Its projection for WTI was also raised to $94 from $81. In a more bullish scenario, Brent could reach $140 a barrel and average around $130 in 2027 if oil production in the Gulf remains 3.5 million barrels per day below its 2025 average, Reuters reported, citing the bank's projections.The bank expects geopolitical uncertainty to contribute a larger risk premium to oil prices. Its projections take into account the possibility of further disruptions to Middle Eastern supplies, the historical length of major supply shocks and the challenges of reaching a durable diplomatic settlement.The forecasts underline how the longer-term trajectory of crude prices remains closely tied to the course of the conflict, even as expectations of higher exports continue to put pressure on prices in the near term.JPMorgan analysts have similarly cautioned that the conflict remains difficult to predict, making its potential fallout hard to assess. The bank had initially expected the US administration to avoid crossing certain economic thresholds. However, seven months into the conflict, several of these thresholds have been breached, while a clear plan to bring the war to an end remains absent.According to JPMorgan, oil markets are likely to remain caught between the threat of supply disruptions and the industry's ability to offset their impact.In its base-case scenario, the bank expects Middle Eastern oil supplies to stay above their 2025 average. This would be supported by measures such as ship-to-ship transfers and additional pipeline capacity. At the same time, production growth in other parts of the world is expected to come to a standstill.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. item.title: South Korea's central bank resumes tightening with quarter-point hike
item.description: The Bank of Korea raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point to 3.25%. This increase follows a pause in October and is part of the tightening cycle. Economic growth has been upgraded to 3.9% for this year and 4.1% for next year. Policymakers remain cautious due to elevated inflation and a heated housing market.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Korea on Thursday raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point to 3.25%, resuming its tightening cycle after a pause in October as a chip-driven export boom keeps inflation and housing prices elevated.The seven-member monetary policy board voted to raise the seven-day repurchase rate to its highest level since November 2024, a decision forecast by 32 of 34 analysts surveyed by Reuters.The bank also raised this year's growth forecast to 3.9% from 3.3% previously, and saw a 4.1% expansion next year, up from 2.9% previously. That would be the fastest growth since 2021 when the economy grew 4.7%.The bank also saw stickier inflation for 2027, at 2.4%, up from 2.3% previously.It was the BOK's third rate hike this year, following back-to-back increases in July and August, and brought cumulative tightening to 75 basis points.Asia's fourth-largest economy has expanded faster than anticipated in 2026 on surging global demand for semiconductors. Policymakers remained on a hawkish footing amid a heated housing market and headline inflation hovering near 3%, well above the BOK's 2% target.At its previous meeting on October 22, the central bank held rates steady at 3.00% to assess external risks and the lagging impact of its summer hikes, while sharply upgrading its economic growth projections for both this year and next.BOK Governor Shin Hyun Song, who last month said the bank will take a data-dependent approach rather than a fixed rate trajectory, is scheduled to hold a news conference at 0210 GMT to explain the board's decision and unveil updated quarterly economic projections.

item.title: S&P warns Nvidia's board may be compromised, puts chipmaker's rating on downgrade watch
item.description: The move comes amid a turbulent period for Nvidia's leadership. The company's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang earlier this week, days after he resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs with his direct reports as well as a Chinese businesswoman alleged by US intelligence to be Beijing's spy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade on Wednesday, saying the departure and subsequent reinstatement of its CEO had exposed weaknesses in the chipmaker's management and board oversight. We believe the long tenure of certain board members may have compromised their independence. The company's corporate governance practices may also not have kept pace with Nvidia's rapid growth and its role as a critical global technology enabler, the ratings agency said.The move comes amid a turbulent period for Nvidia's leadership. The company's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang earlier this week, days after he resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs with his direct reports as well as a Chinese businesswoman alleged by US intelligence to be Beijing's spy.Critics and lawmakers slammed the reinstatement, questioning the independence of the board, whose newly elected chair had told investors last week Nvidia would not rehire Huang as CEO because his personal behavior was inconsistent with the company's code of conduct.Reinstating Huang on Monday, Nvidia omitted any mention of his affairs, saying instead the move was based on US government input, even as an independent board committee continued its investigation into reports involving him and a suspected foreign intelligence effort.Reuters reported on Wednesday that the US Justice Department did not conduct a formal investigation into Huang before US President Donald Trump pushed for his return as CEO, according to three people familiar with the matter.Instead, it concluded that there was no evidence he had broken any laws based on ongoing investigations into two Nvidia clients, Super Micro and Megaspeed International, which are suspected of smuggling advanced microchips to China. That determination is subject to change as the probes continue.NO EVIDENCE YET THAT ALICE HUANG IS A SPYInvestors were largely unruffled by the S&P move, which comes with Nvidia shares down 38% since October 6. Nvidia closed down nearly 4% on Wednesday, retracing some declines after the Nasdaq 100 index briefly flirted with a 20% decline from its recent high.The cost of insurance against tech companies defaulting on debts has jumped sharply in recent weeks, but the five-year CDS spread for Nvidia was little changed.Nvidia currently has an 'AA' rating, which indicates a very strong capacity to meet financial commitments. The highest rating is 'AAA'.The agency said it could downgrade Nvidia within the next 90 days, but expects any potential downgrade to be limited to one notch, unless investigations and other disclosures harm the company's reputation or future business prospects.Nvidia has played a key role in financing the AI boom, bankrolling AI startups, cloud firms and data-center projects, which in turn spend much of that capital on Nvidia's own GPUs and other AI chips.The complex financing arrangements have increased Nvidia's exposure to a potential downturn, analysts said.Separately, the Wall Street Journal on Wednesday reported that US officials found no evidence that tech executive Alice Huang was directed by Beijing to spy on Jensen Huang, citing people familiar with a classified briefing.Officials from the CIA, FBI, Office of the Director of National Intelligence and National Security Agency briefed staff from congressional intelligence committees and chamber leaders, the Journal reported.The officials said Alice Huang contacted China's spy agency during the affair but found no indication that she provided significant intelligence, the Journal reported.Nvidia and the agencies did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Reuters could not independently verify the report.The report said current evidence suggests Alice Huang and Jensen Huang may have had an amorous relationship, but it was not a coordinated play by China, and that new information could change that assessment.The briefing also noted that Kang Wei, described to the Journal as Alice Huang's husband by people who know them, was an asset for China's Ministry of State Security who remained in frequent contact with the intelligence service.
